pick.name: AWS Marketplace
pick.why: Biggest enterprise procurement channel; seller eligibility depends on entity country
pick.free_limits: No upfront listing cost; fee on each sale: 3% for public SaaS offers; private offers 3% (<USD 1M TCV), 2% (USD 1-10M), 1.5% (>= USD 10M); renewals 1.5%; regional uplifts may apply (e.g. India-based sellers)

alts.name: Microsoft Marketplace (transactable SaaS)
alts.what: List SaaS so enterprises buy against their Microsoft agreement
alts.why: Flat 3% store fee; Microsoft bills and collects

alts.name: Google Cloud Marketplace
alts.why: Needs Partner Network membership and GCP-hosted product

candidates.name: Salesforce AppExchange
candidates.verdict: Relevant if you sell to Salesforce customers; not checked

candidates.name: Snowflake Marketplace
candidates.verdict: Relevant for data products; not checked

decision: Defer marketplaces until an enterprise buyer asks, then list where that buyer's committed cloud spend sits. Microsoft's 3% transact model is simple; AWS has the widest reach. Seller eligibility depends on the legal entity and country.
details: No free option: marketplaces take a revenue share or listing fee on every sale; listing itself is free only until you transact.

region_notes.US: US entities have the broadest seller eligibility on all three marketplaces.
region_notes.India: AWS Marketplace supports India-based sellers (since Nov 2025) but they can sell only to buyers in India; global AWS sales need a non-India entity. Microsoft payout/tax profile for India publishers not confirmed.

verify.note: Checked against primary sources; wording made neutral during verification.
